sources.title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning
inspected_locations: PDF p.3 §3.1 Eqs.(1)-(2), including actual page render
PDF p.4 §3.2 (boundary: learned rather than fixed codebook)
excerpts:
We define a latent embedding space e ∈ RK×D where K is the size of the discrete latent space (i.e.,
a K-way categorical), and D is the dimensionality of each latent embedding vector ei . Note that
there are K embedding vectors ei ∈ RD , i ∈ 1, 2, ..., K. As shown in Figure 1, the model takes an
input x, that is passed through an encoder producing output ze (x). The discrete latent variables z
are then calculated by a nearest neighbour look-up using the shared embedding space e as shown in
equation 1. The input to the decoder is the corresponding embedding vector ek as given in equation 2.

The prior distribution over the discrete latents p(z) is a categorical distribution, and can be made
autoregressive by depending on other z in the feature map. Whilst training the VQ-VAE, the prior is
kept constant and uniform. After training, we fit an autoregressive distribution over z, p(z), so that
we can generate x via ancestral sampling. We use a PixelCNN over the discrete latents for images,
and a WaveNet for raw audio. Training the prior and the VQ-VAE jointly, which could strengthen our
results, is left as future research.
sources.inspection_note: Eqs.(1)-(2) select the minimum L2-distance embedding and feed that same embedding to the decoder. Squaring the nonnegative L2 distance preserves argmin. Lesson uses zero-based IDs and fixed raw-sample vectors; it does not claim to implement the paper’s learned encoder, objective or learned prior. §3.3 independently fits a prior over codes for generation.

sources.title: SoundStream: An End-to-End Neural Audio Codec
inspected_locations: PDF pp.1-2 Introduction and Fig.2 caption
excerpts:
A convolutional encoder produces a latent representation of the input audio samples,
which is quantized using a variable number nq of residual vector quantizers (RVQ).

The encoded audio enc(x) ∈ RS×D is then mapped
      ŷ += Qi (residual)                                        to a sequence of one-hot vectors of shape S × N , which can
      residual −= Qi (residual)                                  be represented using S log2 N bits.
sources.inspection_note: The first excerpt is the original Fig.2 caption. §III explicitly separates encoder embeddings, quantized embeddings and a lossy waveform decoder. §III-A gives frames spanning many raw samples. This supports the lesson’s neural audio-codec abstraction; it does not establish that every non-neural audio codec uses learned feature codebooks. The extraction contains two-column interleaving; the model description and its headings were read in context.

sources.title: Simple and Controllable Music Generation
inspected_locations: PDF pp.2-3 §2 Method and §2.1 Audio tokenization
PDF p.4 §2.3 Model conditioning and §2.4 Transformer decoder
excerpts:
M USIC G EN consists in an autoregressive transformer-based decoder [Vaswani et al., 2017], condi-
tioned on a text or melody representation. The (language) model is over the quantized units from
an EnCodec [Défossez et al., 2022] audio tokenizer, which provides high fidelity reconstruction
from a low frame rate discrete representation.

Text conditioning. Given a textual description matching the input audio X, we compute a condi-
tioning tensor C ∈ RTC ×D with D being the inner dimension used in the autoregressive model.
sources.inspection_note: Separates the audio tokenizer/reconstruction from a text-conditioned autoregressive model over quantized audio units. Used only to verify the distinction between reconstruction inputs and learned conditional code generation; no MusicGen performance or this toy’s generation ability is inferred.

sources.title: PyTorch official broadcasting semantics
inspected_locations: General semantics: trailing dimensions and maximum result dimension
excerpts:
Two tensors are "broadcastable" if the following rules hold:

- When iterating over the dimension sizes, starting at the trailing dimension,
  the dimension sizes must either be equal, one of them is 1, or one of them
  does not exist.

If two tensors `x`, `y` are "broadcastable", the resulting tensor size
is calculated as follows:

- If the number of dimensions of `x` and `y` are not equal, prepend 1
  to the dimensions of the tensor with fewer dimensions to make them equal length.
- Then, for each dimension size, the resulting dimension size is the max of the sizes of
  `x` and `y` along that dimension.
sources.inspection_note: Read the pinned official note. [3,1,4] and [1,3,4] yield [3,3,4]; reducing its final axis yields [3,3]. CPU execution independently confirms those shapes.
